speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance; can you tell me if these symptoms started suddenly or came on gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: That spinning sensation sounds like vertigo. Did you notice any hearing changes, such as ringing in your ears or muffled hearing, when the dizziness started? Also, do you experience any double vision or slurred speech?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sustained sensation of the room spinning. I also have Occasional nausea, Use of diphenhydramine for symptoms and to aid sleep, Recent cold.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Vestibular Neuritis (likely post-viral etiology following recent cold, characterized by sustained constant vertigo without auditory symptoms).
